A free seat is an easy yes for anyone who reads your books or follows your exercises, and every seat is an email address you keep.

What it really takes to become a somatic breathwork facilitator

A free, live 60-minute class with Rebecca Dennis, founder of Breathing Tree Training, for anyone who loves breathwork and wonders whether guiding others could be their next step.

Rebecca Dennis · Breathing Tree

Who this class is for

Gentle, grounded education. No pressure.

  • People with their own breathwork practice who feel drawn to share it with others.
  • Yoga teachers, coaches and wellbeing professionals who want to understand breathwork facilitation.
  • Anyone curious about what professional facilitator training involves, before committing to one.
  • Anyone who wants to understand the science of the breath more deeply.

Here’s what you’ll learn

Five things we’ll cover in 60 minutes

What a breathwork facilitator actually does

What happens before, during and after a session, and why guiding others is very different from your own practice.

The science, explained simply

The anatomy and physiology of the breath and the basics of the nervous system, without the jargon.

Holding a calm, safe space

Why space holding matters more than technique, and what it looks like with a group.

A gentle practice, guided live

A short, seated breathing practice so you can experience how a session is held. You can simply listen if you prefer.

How to know if you’re ready to train

The experience a good training asks for, what a training pathway looks like, and how to choose one.

Meet Rebecca

Hi, I’m Rebecca Dennis

I’ve been a breathwork practitioner for nearly 20 years. I’m a Somatic Breathwork Trainer, the founder of Breathing Tree Training, and the author of Let It Go, Breathe and And Breathe.

I teach one-to-one in London and online, run workshops and retreats, and train new facilitators through an accredited programme.

Questions

Before you save your seat

Do I need any experience?

No. The class is for anyone curious about breathwork facilitation, whether you practise every day or are just starting out.

Is there a breathing practice?

Yes, one short, gentle, seated practice. You can simply listen if you prefer. Breathwork isn’t suitable for everyone: if you are in the first trimester of pregnancy, have uncontrolled high blood pressure or epilepsy, or are unsure, please check with your doctor first.

Will I have to be on camera?

No. Cameras stay off for attendees, and you can ask questions in the chat.

What if I can’t make it live?

Every seat includes the replay, so you can watch when it suits you.

Is it really free?

Yes. Save your seat with your first name and email.

Educational content, not medical advice. Breathwork is not suitable for everyone. If you are unsure, please check with your doctor before joining the practice.

Script 1 · “More than counting breaths”

Hook (0 to 3s)

“People think a breathwork facilitator just counts breaths. That’s the smallest part of it.”

Body

“The real skill is holding the room: knowing the science, reading the group, and creating a space where people feel safe. I’ve been doing this for nearly 20 years, and that’s what I teach first.”

CTA

“I’m walking through the whole path in a free live masterclass. Replay included. Tap Sign up to save a seat.”

Shot: talking to camera in soft natural light, white wall, calm pace. On-screen text: “more than counting breaths”.

Script 2 · “Before you train”

Hook (0 to 3s)

“Thinking about breathwork facilitator training? Ask these three questions first.”

Body

“One: how much of your own practice do you have? Two: does the training teach the science, not just the technique? Three: will you practise facilitating under supervision before you qualify? I cover all three in my free class.”

CTA

“It’s free and live, with a replay. Tap Sign up below.”

Shot: seated, counting the three questions on fingers. Captions on screen. “Educational content, not medical advice.”

Script 3 · “Three books in”

Hook (0 to 3s)

“I’ve written three books about the breath. Here’s what I teach every new facilitator first.”

Body

“Your own practice comes before anyone else’s. Then the science: anatomy, physiology, the nervous system. Then space holding. In my free masterclass I’ll show you the full path, and guide a short, gentle practice so you can feel how a session is held.”

CTA

“Save your free seat. Tap Sign up.”

Shot: holding the three books, then cut to Rebecca guiding a seated breath. Caption: “Educational content, not medical advice.”
